Assembly Builder — reading THE library. The window is live: pick one of the seeded assemblies, switch its element class, edit thicknesses, add and remove layers — the section preview, dims and totals follow. Every number comes from the app's own materials.json (181 materials: λ, ρ, the three ECI lines and which one the Σ reads, the biogenic line, the EPD source, note and ✓) and assemblies.json (the 104 seeded assemblies), embedded verbatim at build — the same files the app ships. The provenance strip under the layers lists, per layer, the value used and the document it came from. Biogenic carbon is its own line (never folded into a sum unless you tick it), and prices show only where the library carries one — pricing is a separate arc.

How the cost row is computed — and why it mostly says "unpriced" today.

One basis stated, two derived. A per-kg price reaches m³ through the material's density; a per-m² price through its slice thickness; missing density → n/a, never 0.

$1 means unknown. Every material ships at $1 until curated — the cell says ⚠ unpriced, the assembly leaves that layer out and prints (n of N unpriced) in the unit slot. Today only the three SIGA membranes carry a real price (Andy, 2026-09-06).

Labour, P&O and tax are multipliers, per material — labour 1.00 = equal to material, P&O 0.20, HST 0.13. Never a hidden constant.

Live. Change a price here and the swatch cost above follows — the same in-memory library.
Same library, app and web. build_assembly_builder.py pastes the seed's materials.json and assemblies.json verbatim between two markers in this file, so the page carries exactly what the app ships (the artifact sandbox cannot fetch). A hosted copy — the OBJECTIVE energy-modelling site — leaves the markers empty and drops the two JSON files beside the page: the same script then fetches them by name. One source, two readers, no second data store.
The metric rows compute from each material's Physical Properties as the app does. ECI folds each layer by the line the material's Σ reads (INSPECTOR-2 §2.4): per kg → t × ρ × EC, per m³ → t × EC/m³ (insulation, wood, concrete, masonry), per m² → the declared m² whatever the thickness (membranes, tile, carpet, paint). Members weight by area fraction (width ÷ spacing). Nominal RSI = Σ t ÷ λ + the ISO 6946 air films for the class and exposure (Rsi 0.13 wall · 0.10 roof · 0.17 floor; Rse 0.04; ground contact drops Rse); air spaces use a tabulated R. Airtightness Req. is STATED, never computed (the OBOA cheatsheet rows).
Biogenic carbon is a separate line item (Andy 2026-09-06: "I do not like it when other apps spoon feed curated combined values as it is hard to know what is what from a Sum"). The ECI row is GWP-fossil A1–A3; the row beneath is the store the EPD declares (negative = carbon held in the product: Gutex −280/m³, cellulose −89/m³, the straw panel −298/m³). Tick Σ + biogenic to see the combined figure — the app does the same per material through its biogenic_in_sum toggle, off by default.
The provenance strip is the footer Andy asked for: per layer, the material, the Σ line it contributes on and its value, the biogenic line, the EPD it was read from (declaration, dates — the first clause of the material's note), a ✓ where the value was verified against the document on its declared basis, PROXY / EXPIRED where the note says so, and the price where one exists. Hover a document for the whole note; the source is a link where it is a URL. 137 of the 172 real materials are verified (2026-09-06); the rest say why.
Orientation and reference are the rulings, verbatim. Walls & roofs read Outside / Top ↑ … Inside / Bottom ↓; floors flip. The reference face (§5) defaults per class and is the red REF line; thickness grows outward from it. The thin-layer law (Andy 2026-08-30): membranes keep their honest thickness in the data but draw as a thick dashed line — the library's representation: "line" flag. Members are first-class sub-rows (the UBAKUS grouping): ⌶ on a layer opens a member with its own material, width and spacing; wood in a cavity draws as end grain, wood in an airspace as a strapping rectangle. Steel is linework (Andy 2026-09-06: a gauge thickness draws as one thick line, never solid geometry or two skins): in a batt cavity the C-stud (web across the depth, 1⅝″ flanges, ½″ lips), in an airspace the hat channel (brims on the substrate face, the crown spanning the depth to the cladding), through continuous rigid insulation the Z-girt. Centreline reference = the centre of the structure, not of the whole assembly (Andy 2026-09-15). Solid mass wins outright — the thickest contiguous run of concrete, masonry or mass timber deeper than 140 mm, measured over its full depth, so a topping bonded to a slab is one portion and five CLT plies are one panel. Failing that, the framed cavity at or above 88.9 mm (a 2×4 on the flat, the shallowest structural system with a centreline): the depth floor is what retires the strapped rainscreen void, which has a member but is not a structural system. A layer marked ◉ CORE overrides all of it — one per assembly, the radio beside its thickness — and Centreline was split into Centre of Structure and Centre of Assembly so the two can never be confused again.
Not here: applying an assembly to geometry, per-layer solids, dewpoint / moisture / full wbLCA (the OBJECTIVE tier this page will feed), and pricing beyond what the library already carries.

⚠ Cost Disclaimer

Prices cited are drawn from public-facing resources, date cited: September 16, 2026, and are intended to assist with budgetary pricing for early planning only. General Contractors and/or Quantity Surveyors shall be responsible for all assembly-level pricing beyond Schematic Design, which this app is intended to assist with.

How a total is built. Commercial construction benchmarks the final contract price of a standard project as 40 % materials & equipment / 40 % labour (fully burdened) / 20 % overhead & profit. This app follows that benchmark: the material rate is doubled to cover labour to give direct costs, which then carry a 25 % markup — equivalently, division by 0.80 — so that O&P is 20 % of the final price. (A 25 % markup is a 20 % margin; a 20 % markup would leave only 16.7 %.) 13 % HST (Ontario) is added on top. It is a budgeting benchmark, not a quotation, and it makes no assumption about how any contractor prices their own work.

Many factors are not covered here, and each can move a real price substantially: season and weather premiums, market conditions and escalation, discounts for bulk purchase, transportation and site access, labour availability, project scale and procurement route, among others. Pricing is subject to significant differences in every market and at every date.

OpenBuilding (the entity that will host the web app) assumes NO LIABILITY for any values listed in this app — thermal, cost, wbLCA or otherwise. Practitioners and users must use their own professional judgement and verify any and all data for accuracy themselves. The information furnished here is for educational value only and is not fit for any other purpose.
